rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial construction for excluding A from a group.

example.english: Everyone has to work except me, but I have the day off today.
example.traditional: 除咗我之外，個個都要返工，但係我今日放假。
example.jyutping: ceoi4 zo2 ngo5 zi1 ngoi6 go3 go3 dou1 jiu3 faan1 gung1 daan6 hai6 ngo5 gam1 jat6 fong3 gaa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for contrasting one clause or idea with another.

example.english: I want to go, but it's raining today.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 heoi3 daan6 hai6 gam1 jat6 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Use this for a contrasting qualification or a softer “however,” including after a negative statement.

example.english: This restaurant is good, but it’s a bit expensive.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳唔錯，不過價錢貴咗啲。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 m4 co3 bat1 gwo3 gaa3 cin2 gwai3 zo2 di1

rows.note: Use this mainly in the corrective pattern “not A but B,” especially in more formal or careful speech.

example.english: This is not a demand but a suggestion.
example.traditional: 呢個唔係要求，而係建議。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 m4 hai6 jiu1 kau4 ji4 hai6 gin3 ji5
